mine_p12_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_001.text: Day 559 began with rain striking the yard hard enough to erase the cart marks. Lin ate at Han's table before walking to her surface shift. The board carried Fan's new stop notice: the changed drainage condition required assessment, and the old accessible gallery clearance no longer applied to another walk. The scheduled inquiry had already ended. Lin had no reason to enter, whichever assistant task she had chosen earlier. She checked in at the outside receiving shelter and watched Ma Lian organize the ordinary withdrawal from the permitted maintenance positions.

mine_p12_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_002.text: Ou Sheng reported the ventilation condition to the work contact, using the timing source his task required. A returning worker asked whether the strange hum beneath the wall meant the living seam was angry. Ou said he had heard ordinary changes in air and water and had no evidence of a mind. Fan needed those conditions recorded before reassessment. Lin copied the permitted message to its proper receiving reference without adding a prediction. The noise sounded different from the familiar echo, but difference alone did not identify a cause or authorize anyone to follow it.

mine_p12_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_003.text: Ma stood at the maintained stair with the withdrawal roster, letting workers pass one group at a time under the stop plan. The current assigned people did not need to finish their last line before leaving. Lin heard one complain that his tool box remained beyond the closed limit. Ma said its retrieval would wait for qualified clearance. The worker cursed, then came through. Lin understood how expensive the abandoned box might be and saw him choose life without turning the choice into a noble speech. He wanted his tools back and was right to want them.

mine_p12_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_004.text: Qiao checked the outside names against shift sources. The roster did not list every visitor who might happen to be somewhere in the yard. Ren contacted the gate clerk for the separate public receiving count while Ma completed the assigned gallery withdrawal. Lin remained at the receiving shelter, recording ordinary items still allowed on the sound outside route. She could help make a contact line clear. She could not declare an entire workplace empty because her own list looked complete. The bell had not yet rung as an alarm, and everyone still hoped this would be a tedious weather delay.

mine_p12_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_005.text: Lei An arrived carrying a lamp he had taken from active service on instruction. He put it in the outside store rack and asked Lin whether Han had forgiven the carter's shirt yet. She said the shorter sleeve had become the room's most discussed garment. Lei smiled and checked the lamp's ordinary fastening before closing the rack. Lin would remember that small competent action with unreasonable precision afterward. At the time it was another familiar exchange during a wet shift. She expected him to join supper and complain about the roof like everyone else.

mine_p12_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_006.text: A deep knock came from the closed inner side store. Several people stopped speaking. Fan moved to the sound outside observation point with Ma, keeping workers behind the marked limit. He did not ask Lin's body to test the wall. Ou reported a changed water sound, and Qiao ordered the receiving queue held before a loaded cart could approach the suspect connection. Lin set down her count book and repeated the hold instruction to the waiting driver. The room's ordinary work had become an evacuation task without granting her any new qualified role.

mine_p12_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_007.text: The second knock was followed by the noise of timber giving way. Dust pushed from the gallery entrance, then an canopy beside the store shifted toward the yard. Lei was turning away from its rack when a falling member struck the hand he had put against the low rail. Lin saw him drop to one knee. She could not reach the member safely through the moving debris. Ma pulled the nearby workers behind the clear line while the assigned ordinary responders approached through the checked side. The first useful action was to keep others from joining the falling structure.

mine_p12_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_008.text: Lin wanted to spend half a unit before she even knew what task she imagined. The desire felt immediate and almost reasonable: she had learned six pairs, a friend was hurt, and doing nothing seemed unbearable. There was no assessed shoulder or waist application that could catch the overhead member or heal his hand. She stopped the impulse before an input began, took the empty chair Qiao called for, and carried it through the assigned sound path. Ordinary hands could do a particular safe task. That was enough for the next few breaths, though it felt far smaller than love.

mine_p12_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_009.text: Fan isolated the damaged connection and directed the qualified crew's approach. Ma kept the exit free; Ou withdrew the remaining nearby equipment work; Qiao sounded the alarm through the assigned contact. Lin did not invent another evacuation plan beside theirs. She repeated the public hold instruction when a carter tried to move forward for a view. The carter called her officious until another piece struck the ground beyond the line. He then backed away. The danger had become visible, but their first instruction had needed to work before everyone could see its reason.

mine_p12_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_010.text: The crew reached Lei through the checked side and moved him out from the damaged rail. Lin saw his face more clearly than his hand and was grateful for that small mercy. He kept asking whether the lamp had broken. Ma told him the store could wait. The assigned responder covered the actual injury and called the clinic through the prepared message contact. Nobody told him pain meant his meridians were opening or that qi could preserve the crushed tissue. He was a lamp worker with a human injury, and ordinary qualified care was being arranged for him.

mine_p12_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_011.text: Lin brought the chair close enough for the responder to use without crossing the restricted approach. Lei tried to stand by himself, then accepted help. He asked her to tell Han he would be late for supper. She said she would. She did not promise he would be ready to return that evening. The words tasted inadequate beside his fear, yet they were a thing she could actually do. Qiao sent the named runner to Chen Ai's nearby clinic. Lin kept the sound path clear while another worker fetched covering from the assigned response cupboard.

mine_p12_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_012.text: A worker shouted that someone still had to go after Diao Shan. The record steward's gallery source list lay on the covered table, and people had begun confusing the vulnerable papers with his physical location. Qiao asked who had actually seen him that morning. Ren supplied his check in at the outside copy room; the gate clerk confirmed the route he had used to collect a permitted message. Lin stayed out of the argument until she had a source to give. A person's name on a store record did not prove his body remained inside the store.

mine_p12_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_013.text: Diao emerged from the copy room with a soaked envelope beneath his coat. He had heard the alarm but taken the sound back path while Ma closed the damaged front connection. Qiao checked his actual exit and marked him present. The old originals were still in the closed inner store. Diao looked toward it and understood what everyone had been fearing before he spoke. He asked Fan whether retrieval was possible. The engineer said the new condition did not allow it. Diao accepted the answer with a face Lin had never seen, as though a shelf had become a funeral.

mine_p12_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_014.text: The assigned maintenance withdrawal count was complete, but one public messenger remained unconfirmed. Yin Dou had entered the surface gate for a private delivery, not a gallery shift. The receiving clerk's contact note had not recorded his later route. Ren called through the other outside gate rather than putting a searcher into the damaged passage on the strength of a missing line. Lin watched Qiao resist the pressure to announce everyone safe prematurely. Lei was visibly out, the maintenance crew was accounted for, and a visitor's location still needed an actual answer. All three facts could coexist without simplification.

mine_p12_015.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_015.text: Yin came through the sound public gate carrying his unopened parcel. He had been sheltering under the market awning while the delivery contact was absent. The gate clerk confirmed the route and time before Qiao closed that part of the outside count. The delay had frightened his cousin, who struck his shoulder angrily when he finally appeared. Yin protested that no one had told him where to wait. Ren recorded the communication gap for later ordinary correction. Nobody had survived a hidden tunnel. A missing contact line had made a person seem closer to danger than his actual path was.

mine_p12_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_016.text: Chen Ai arrived through the checked outside route twenty minutes after the runner's message, with the ordinary clinic assistant carrying the permitted response kit. She assessed Lei directly and asked the bystanders to make room. Lin obeyed even though stepping away felt like abandoning him. The clinician needed actual access to the injury and the patient, not an audience supplying interpretations. Lei consented to the necessary immediate care and transport arrangement. Chen explained that a qualified hand surgeon would need to assess the crushed tissue. She did not pretend her general clinic role could guarantee a reconstructed hand.

mine_p12_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_017.text: Qiao arranged a licensed cart to the district surgical room along the sound surface road. The journey would take about two hours under the day's conditions, and the road contact checked that the receiving surgeon could see Lei on arrival. Lin would not move a patient through the damaged gallery because it looked shorter. A worker suggested a practitioner might fly him there. No available qualified method in this group supplied that option. They prepared the ordinary transport, its receiving contact, and a companion Lei chose. Ma went with him after the outside evacuation duty passed to its designated relief.

mine_p12_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_018.text: Before leaving Lei asked Lin to keep his ordinary supper place if he returned late. She said Han would know where he had gone and would keep his belongings safe. She could promise custody arrangements she would actually make, not a return time or the survival of fingers she had not been qualified to assess. Lei squeezed her sleeve with his uninjured hand. Then the cart moved out on the checked road, carrying the responder's actual transfer note and Ma as his chosen companion. Lin watched its wheels until the rain turned them into moving shadows beyond the gate.

mine_p12_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_019.text: The damaged canopy remained isolated after the cart left. Fan did not open the closed store merely because the outside names were now accounted for. New water and load conditions required reassessment by the appropriate ordinary crew. Qiao kept all unscheduled retrieval outside the assigned work. The workers with abandoned tools wanted an answer that would save both time and property. Fan could only give the current limit and the next assessment needed. Lin understood their anger better after seeing Lei. It remained possible to care about a tool and refuse to risk another hand in order to recover it.

mine_p12_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_020.text: Sui arrived from the outer receiving line and asked what had caused the failure. Fan said the immediate observations included changed drainage, a giving timber connection, and propagation into the older canopy. They did not yet establish the whole underlying cause. Sui wanted to know whether his rejected damp wedges would be blamed. Those pieces had not entered structural use. The source record mattered and would be checked. Lin refused to turn an anxious question into proof of innocence beyond what the actual disposition supported. A specific excluded bundle did not explain every other member in the structure.

mine_p12_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_021.text: Ou stood beside the covered table with his ventilation timing notes, shaking hard enough to spill his first cup of water. He had withdrawn on instruction and performed the report his task required. Lin gave him a dry cloth, not a cultivation diagnosis. He said the altered hum had sounded like the remembered song for a moment. Lin asked who had been speaking. No one had identified a voice source in that noise. They left it as an unclassified ordinary sound under changed conditions, without naming Lu Sen as its speaker or turning a frightened association into a living return.

mine_p12_022.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_022.text: Diao tried to list the originals in the inner store from memory. Ren asked him to separate known inventory references from pages he only feared might be there. The distinction hurt because Diao wanted the loss to have a complete shape before the damage could be assessed. Lin sat nearby and helped find the permitted location list they had actually discussed. It named some work amendments and private source dependencies, not every word inside every page. They could begin an honest loss inquiry with that record. They could not recover an archive by writing confidently enough on a new sheet.

mine_p12_023.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_023.text: The ordinary receiving shift stopped where the alarm had interrupted it. Qiao recorded the actual completed hours and reassigned the safe remainder to outside contact work under the accepted half day, rather than paying Lin for imaginary completed counts. Lin spent the remaining time carrying permitted messages on the sound path and helping Ren keep the current references separate. The task remained ordinary assistant work for the agreed four copper half day after actual hours. Her private method notebook stayed at Han's room. The accident had changed the work, not earned a certificate or funded her future examination through danger.

mine_p12_024.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_024.text: Chen Rui arrived at the public contact table after the evacuation and asked for the permitted factual disposition. He did not receive private clinical findings because the company retained him for a proposal. Qiao supplied the ordinary incident sources he had authority to review for the employer's response. Luo would handle consenting worker claims through his own appointment. Chen began to say that the mine's swift response demonstrated its readiness. Lin interrupted. Lei was still travelling toward assessment, and the structure's cause remained unresolved. Readiness could not be proved by choosing an attractive sentence before the actual harm was known.

mine_p12_025.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_025.text: Chen looked at her, then crossed the phrase from his note. He said she was right. The admission did not undo his instinct to make the client's response sound complete. Lin had no energy to praise his correction. She asked him to preserve the actual unresolved questions and returned to the contact task. Luo thanked her quietly, without offering a wider mandate than she held. Her earlier advocacy choice had ended; any current source help would still need its own scope. Anger did not give her authority over Lei's private injury or every worker's claim.

mine_p12_026.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_026.text: By midday Qiao assigned a separate finite incident account for immediate qualified care and transport, beginning with the actual clinic response and the accepted surgical referral. It would not borrow the workers' twelve copper unused workshop deposits or Lin's twenty four copper curriculum. Company responsibility for assigned work needed an ordinary paid response even before every cause was established. The surgeon would specify what treatment was actually needed, and later costs would require their own defined arrangement. Lin listened for the funded receiving contact rather than a promise that kindness would somehow make medical labor available without payment.

mine_p12_027.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_027.text: Qiao reserved ninety six company coppers for the immediate arrangement after the receiving clinic confirmed its local charges. Eight paid Chen Ai's response; thirty two covered Zhao's assessment and ordinary surgical treatment with the first overnight care and assigned dressings. Eight reserved the surgeon's Day 561 followup, and eight the local clinic followup planned for Day 564. Qualified contacts supplied the actual local charges. Lei consented to actual care; unused reservations stayed unspent.

mine_p12_028.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_028.text: The same account covered six for Lei's subsequent room and meals on Days 560 through 562, and eight for Ma's four days as his chosen companion. Sixteen bought two licensed cart legs, outward now and return on Day 563 if suitable. Six booked the two visitors' return tickets Lei requested; four covered actual contact messages and permitted transfer copies. Together the defined care, board, transport, visit, and messages used the ninety six allocation. None required Lin to spend the personal reserve her own body might later need.

mine_p12_029.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_029.text: Ren checked the account with the authorized company clerk while Lin carried the contact reply. The money had been assigned from an existing incident reserve and its receiving payments were accepted; it was not a debt Lei had to earn off through damaged work. Lost outside opportunities and abandoned property would still need their own factual claims. Qiao said the first responsibility was getting the actual person to qualified care. Lin could follow the funded task from this room to the receiving room, without mistaking it for his whole future.

mine_p12_030.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_030.text: Fan's outside assessment found damage extending beyond the first visible connection. He kept the inner store and adjacent approach closed. The qualified crew installed only the ordinary temporary isolation allowed from the sound side, with no retrieval attempt included. Lin watched workers place a warning far enough back that a curious visitor would meet it before seeing the dramatic broken canopy. One worker wanted the sign closer so people could admire how serious it looked. Ma's relief said the point was stopping them early, not making the danger's best viewing position official. The sign stayed on the useful line.

mine_p12_031.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_031.text: The rain slackened and sunlight briefly struck the red spoils. Several workers took that as a sign the worst was over. Fan said dry light did not reverse soaked material, load changes, or the failed member. He would assess the new condition through ordinary sources rather than letting the sky certify it. Lin looked at the bright wet ground and felt her own wish to believe him unnecessary. A friend had gone away hurt; everyone wanted the day to begin resolving itself. The visible world supplied a scene and no new qualified evidence about Lei's hand or the closed store.

mine_p12_032.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_032.text: At the covered table Ren received the district room's acknowledgement that Lei and Ma had actually arrived after the ordinary two hour journey. The note did not claim a completed operation. It named Surgeon Zhao Lan as the qualified receiving practitioner and confirmed Lei's consent to assessment. Lin read only the transfer disposition Lei had permitted for the workplace contact. His private findings would stay under medical custody unless he chose a particular disclosure. She carried the permitted arrival news to Han so the lodging would know where its lamp worker was. The message was narrow, true, and desperately welcome.

mine_p12_033.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_033.text: Han listened without interrupting, then put Lei's sleeping mat away from the damp window. He wanted to know whether the hand would heal. Lin said the qualified assessment was still underway. Han looked angry at the unanswered question and then thanked her for not inventing an answer. He reserved the bed under Lei's paid lodging arrangement and asked the work contact about later board if recovery kept him away. Lin did not offer to cover an indefinite rent she could not afford. She could protect his things that night and make sure the question reached someone authorized to answer it.

mine_p12_034.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_034.text: Mu came in carrying her repaired screen tools and stopped when she saw the unused supper place. Lin told her the permitted public facts. Mu set the tools down before asking how close Lin had been. The answer came out in pieces: the lamp, the knock, the rail, the chair, the cart. Mu let the pieces stay uneven. She did not demand a brave account of perfect choices. Lin had wanted to do something impossible with half a unit. Saying that aloud made her shake more, then less, because the wish no longer had to hide behind a useful task.

mine_p12_035.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_035.text: Mu asked whether Lin had actually begun an input. She had not. The distinction mattered for her body record and did not make the wish harmless as a future temptation. Lin would tell Wei at the next appropriate appointment, not ask Mu to examine a route she was not qualified to assess. That evening she needed food, ordinary company, and sleep if sleep came. Han brought the meal covered by her room arrangement. The spoon felt heavy in a way no quantity measurement described. Lin ate slowly while listening for a message nobody could send before it existed.

mine_p12_036.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_036.text: Lei's authorized result arrived from the district room through the named contact. Zhao had assessed extensive crushing and found two fingers' tissue nonviable. Lei had consented to the ordinary surgical treatment recommended for the actual injury. There was no safe available procedure in this room that would restore those fingers. The immediate treatment preserved the viable hand and addressed the injury within the surgeon's qualification. Lin read the short message twice. Qualified care had done real work, and a real permanent loss remained. The two facts were not enemies that a hopeful sentence could force apart.

mine_p12_037.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_037.text: She remembered Lei checking the lamp fastening with both hands that morning. The memory grew sharper than she wanted. No existing route method taught her to recreate tissue, and the new small circuit curriculum did not offer it. She could become more qualified at her own bounded tasks and still be unable to give those fingers back. The limit felt unbearable because it belonged to someone she loved, not because it was unclear. Mu sat beside her without turning the pain into a lesson. For a while the only useful sound was another person breathing normally in the same room.

mine_p12_038.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_038.text: Han put the reserved supper aside when it became clear Lei would remain in the district room overnight under the agreed immediate care arrangement. He did not pretend the bed at the lodging had housed a patient who was elsewhere. Qiao's contact would settle the actual short medical board and later lodging needs by their own terms. Lin kept Lei's ordinary belongings together, including the strap he had repaired by lamplight days earlier. The buckle still worked. It would become a reminder of what his hands had done, without promising what the changed hand could do next.

mine_p12_039.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_039.text: At the clinic contact window next morning, Lin delivered the permitted lodging message rather than asking to read the private surgical file. Chen Ai confirmed the practical transfer arrangement was complete and would coordinate only the ordinary followup she was actually qualified to provide. Zhao retained the surgical findings and tissue decisions. Lei would choose what employment duty advice could be sent to Qiao when assessed. Lin's love did not make her the owner of his record. She disliked standing outside a room that knew more, and stayed outside until he invited an appropriate visit.

mine_p12_040.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_040.text: The public incident note still had unresolved cause questions. Fan would examine drainage and loading through safe access when available, Ou would supply his actual timing evidence, and the material dispositions would be checked against source custody. The failure had not proved the moths prophetic or the miner's song alive. It had proved that a workplace with ordinary procedures could still suffer a dangerous changing condition and needed an actual response. Lin helped Ren keep observations distinct from inference. A false complete explanation would give people relief today and a worse beginning for tomorrow's work.

mine_p12_041.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_041.text: Several workers accused Sui of supplying rotten timber. He demanded the rejected wedge references be read aloud. Qiao arranged the factual check through the public work contact rather than holding a trial over supper. The particular damp bundle had remained excluded from structural use. Other material and load questions were still open. Sui could be angry at a false accusation while the company still owed an honest structural inquiry. Lin saw how fear wanted one owner for the whole day. The actual sources would produce a less convenient account, and the workers needed that account more than a satisfying villain.

mine_p12_042.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_042.text: Luo gathered consented claims about interrupted assigned work and abandoned private tools. Each owner named their own property and source evidence. A person who lacked a receipt did not automatically lack an object; a remembered claim did not automatically establish every price. Lin did not turn receiving experience into authority to settle them all. She offered the permitted inquiry reference she actually held when it became relevant, keeping its source position clear. The fuller consequences of her chosen task would emerge in the loss review. For now, ordinary people had forms to begin and property they could not retrieve.

mine_p12_043.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_043.text: One worker wanted to reenter at dusk because the gallery seemed quieter. Fan refused. Silence did not restore a connection or establish the inner roof's condition. The worker said the box contained tools that had paid for his children's meals. Fan said that made its loss serious, not its retrieval safe. Qiao asked the owner to register the claim through Luo instead of leaving him with a shouted prohibition. Lin watched him put down the borrowed lamp he had meant to carry inside. The tools stayed beyond the line. His household problem came back into the sound yard with him.

mine_p12_044.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_044.text: Diao brought the limited store inventory to the contact table again, this time with private source owners named only where permission allowed. He had begun to accept that some originals might not be recovered. Lin asked what could still be known from authorized external references. Diao distinguished ordinary totals, a few duplicated work amendments, and individual remembered statements. None recreated every private word or lost detail. The difference would matter to claims and future histories. A careful inquiry could preserve fragments without pretending an archive was whole because people were determined not to lose it.

mine_p12_045.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_045.text: On Day 561 the second eight week assistant block reached its agreed end. Lin had performed the sixteen half days across that block, including safe reassigned contact hours during the incident, for sixty four wages. Thirty two paid its eight weekly board and meal charges. Together with the first block's remainder after curriculum, that left forty from common mine wages saved through these two blocks, apart from her earlier purse and expenses. The arithmetic felt painfully small beside Lei's injury. It was still her money, and she would need it for choices the company could not make inside her body.

mine_p12_046.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_046.text: Qiao offered the next four weeks of ordinary assistant shifts through Day 589 at the same two half days weekly, four coppers each. The task now stayed on the sound outside lines while gallery work was suspended. Lin accepted the actual schedule and asked that study appointments remain visible to the clerk. No emergency loyalty bonus or future certificate wage appeared in the terms. She wanted to remain useful near the people she knew and keep a finite personal reserve. The mine's incident account paid its defined response; her employment still paid work she actually did.

mine_p12_047.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_047.text: Wei sent an appointment question through Guan rather than arriving as an unrequested healer. She wanted to know whether Lin had actually used input during the alarm, experienced a body change, or needed to postpone supervised preparation because sleep and attention were poor. Lin answered the factual portion and requested a later recovered teaching interval. No route injury had been established merely by the frightening wish. No healthy condition could be assumed from not using qi either. Wei accepted the postponement under the course's unused appointment terms and asked Lin to report any new symptom to the proper qualified person.

mine_p12_048.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_048.text: At Han's room Lin read the rehearsal sheet and found she could not hold attention on it. Every blank continuation became a rail beneath Lei's hand. She closed the book before practice and sat beside the window with a cup. A stopped learning evening did not spend input or qualify a route. It also did not resolve her growing urgency. She wanted a method that could make her useful before the next harm, and the wish was beginning to use Lei's injury as an argument for speed. She wrote that plainly, because it frightened her more than an incomplete diagram.

mine_p12_049.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_049.text: Mu read the sentence when Lin offered it and asked whether becoming more skilled would return the fingers. Lin said no. Mu asked whether it would prevent every future injury at the mine. Lin said no again, more sharply. The questions hurt because Lin knew the answers and wanted a different world. Mu did not ask her to abandon study. She asked her to keep the actual task distinct from the wound it could not fix. Lin put the page away and agreed to postpone unfamiliar work until the supervised lesson. The promise would later face pressure of its own.

mine_p12_050.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_050.text: A visit to Lei was arranged after Zhao's ordinary care instructions allowed it and Lei asked for Lin and Mu. They travelled on the booked road service, taking the actual two hour journey. The free interval and two return tickets from the separate company incident account protected Lin's personal wage reserve. She brought no cultivation portion, only Han's authorized message and a cloth pouch Mu had made as a gift. The covered hand belonged to a person, not an invitation to demonstrate hope. Lei would choose what company he wanted when they arrived.

mine_p12_051.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_051.text: At the district doorway Lin hesitated before the permitted visit. She had brought the message and knew where to put it, but could not decide what expression a friend should wear. Mu said Lei could choose whether to talk once they entered. Lin did not need to prepare the perfect face. That was a mercy no examiner could measure. She took an ordinary breath, left her imagined rescue outside, and followed the attendant into the room as the person Lei had actually asked to see.

mine_p12_052.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_052.text: Lei greeted them by asking whether anyone had finally moved the drying line. Lin said it had been moved. He smiled, then looked at the covered hand as if the joke had taken him somewhere he could not follow. He knew the surgical result and did not need Lin to explain it. Mu asked whether he wanted the pouch beside the bed or taken back. He wanted it within reach of the uninjured hand. The ordinary choice made room for him to decide one thing after a day when many things had been decided by damage.

mine_p12_053.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_053.text: He asked whether she could learn to do anything about a hand later. Lin answered the limit: her present method did not heal or recreate tissue, and the small circuit course was not a treatment. She could learn bounded work without promising this impossible repair. Lei nodded and looked disappointed. Honesty did not spare either person the pain. It spared him a false expectation attached to someone else's ambition. He asked her to keep studying anyway, because he liked hearing about the ridiculous benches. Lin laughed and cried at the same moment, which he accepted without trying to manage either.

mine_p12_054.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_054.text: The surgeon's attendant ended the visit at the prescribed interval. Lin stood when asked rather than treating affection as a reason the patient should lose rest. Lei allowed a practical duty update to be sent later after assessment, but did not authorize a public account of every surgical detail. Lin would tell Han only what he wanted known. The private result had reached her through his consent and the permitted contact, not through advocacy or inquiry access. She left the pouch within his reach and carried the room key back as a symbol of a life still waiting for him.

mine_p12_055.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_055.text: On the return journey Mu fell asleep against the cart side. Lin watched fields pass and heard the wheel cross repaired ruts. No distant event became nearer merely because it was urgent. The two hours remained two hours, and a care arrangement needed someone at its receiving end before departure. She thought about stories in which a practitioner arrived at the right breath with the right power. Useful help here had come through people, money, roads, and imperfect timing. The missing fingers belonged to that truthful account, a loss she carried through each ordinary mile.

mine_p12_056.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_056.text: Afterward she found the pouch's unused wrapping in her sleeve. Mu had hemmed the cloth neatly; one corner carried a crooked stitch she had left because it held. Lin folded it rather than throwing it away. The little imperfection belonged to work a living person had done for another living person. It had not repaired the hand or reduced the seriousness of the loss. It had made a gift that could be opened with the uninjured hand, at a moment when that particular use mattered.

mine_p12_057.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_057.text: Han listened to Lei's chosen update and kept the private detail out of the meal room discussion. He asked about the practical lodging plan because an empty bed and a district recovery room were both real costs. Qiao's assigned contact had a finite immediate arrangement and would seek the next actual advice before changing it. Lin did not promise unlimited company coverage or offer money she needed for her own possible care. She helped put Lei's clothes where he had requested. Ordinary custody could be done well without pretending it was the whole answer to his changed future.

mine_p12_058.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_058.text: The yard sounded different after the failure. A hammer knock made people pause; a cart wheel slipping on wet stone drew immediate eyes. Some caution was useful, and some ordinary fear made unrelated work harder. Qiao asked Ma and Fan to explain the current marked limits rather than telling everyone to be brave. Lin watched a worker resume a sound task after hearing the specific condition. Confidence could be rebuilt through an observed permission smaller than general safety. She hoped her own learning would follow that pattern, though her impatience still wanted a single act to make fear disappear.

mine_p12_059.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_059.text: A trader near the market awning began selling fragments as evidence of the seam's warning. Jia said no permitted source established that claim, and the ordinary incident inquiry still had open cause questions. Lin repeated the public limits when asked, without claiming to inspect or certify the trader's goods. The dead worker's song, unidentified hum, moth response, and timber failure remained distinct sources. A story joining them might sell well. It would leave the actual people responsible for ordinary work trying to answer an imaginary witness instead of the conditions they could measure and change.

mine_p12_060.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_060.text: Diao brought a small authorized duplicate out from the outside cabinet and held it like a fragile bowl. It preserved one old work amendment and its source reference. Lin was glad it existed and watched him resist calling it the archive saved. Other originals remained in the damaged closed store. Some words might be permanently gone. He put the duplicate back under its proper custody and began the next limited inventory request. A fragment could support a particular claim without becoming an excuse to declare every loss recovered. The inquiry would need patience as well as grief.

mine_p12_061.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_061.text: The next morning Lin stood at the receiving shelter and looked toward the isolated canopy. She had been outside during the failure, carried a chair, repeated an instruction, and resisted an unassessed qi impulse. Those actions were real and smaller than the rescue she had wished to perform. Lei had received qualified care and lost two fingers. Tools and private pages remained beyond a closed line. The mine would now have to pay, investigate, and adapt without rewriting the day into triumph. Lin opened the permitted work count and began with the first sound item actually before her.

mine_p12_062.speaker: narrator
mine_p12_062.text: At the end of her shift the public loss review notice was ready. It asked owners for abandoned property, sources for authorized surviving references, and workers for consenting accounts of interrupted work. Lin's inquiry role would determine which evidence she could bring firsthand and which she could only report. The decision had not protected everyone from harm or made all knowledge equal after it. She folded the notice beneath the reference she owned and left the private method book alone. The next part of the mine's life would begin with what was truly lost and what could still be known.
